finding: callAsync was converted from `async` to a plain arrow, so its synchronous prologue (`params instanceof FormData` with no global FormData, a throwing token provider, a localStorage read refused in a sandboxed iframe) now throws SYNCHRONOUSLY instead of rejecting — every `ApiClient.X.y(...).catch(...)` call site in all three consuming apps loses that error path.

An entry is only removed when its promise settles and the transport sets no fetch timeout, so a hung GET pins its key forever; on a quiet page the epoch never moves either, making that endpoint permanently unreadable for the session. Before coalescing each caller got its own attempt and a remount recovered.

Joiners receive the SAME parsed object by identity, so N stores now alias one array/object where each previously owned a private parse. Any in-place normalization (sort/push/an immer draft assigning the same reference) silently cross-contaminates unrelated stores. The module header argues safety only in terms of timing, never aliasing.

JSON.stringify does NOT throw on a function/Map/Set/class instance — it emits null/{} — so the catch fallback never fires for the case its own comment names, and two cold-window calls carrying DIFFERENT callbacks both key to "[null]": the second caller is handed the first's promise and its callback never runs.

The cold-window de-dup is applied to EVERY lazy action including MUTATIONS, directly contradicting the transport's own stated rule that a mutation must never be silently collapsed. Two genuine identical invocations in that window (a double-clicked create/delete, two components dispatching the same action) collapse into ONE call and BOTH callers resolve successfully, so the dropped intent is invisible.
A rejected chunk load is memoized forever by `implPromise ??=` and implReady never flips, so a transient chunk 404/network blip permanently bricks the action with no reset path.

The 429 branch ignores currentBackoffMs, so after the transient ladder has escalated to 30s a capacity refusal SHORTENS the wait to ~10-15s — retrying FASTER against an endpoint that just said 'no room' — and repeated 429s never escalate at all. Contradicts the file's own 'never slower than the existing worst case' claim.

noteMeLoaded stamps currentFetchEpoch() at RESPONSE time, the inverse of the guard `coalesce` gets right (epoch captured BEFORE start()). A /me already on the wire when a mutation completes is recorded with the POST-mutation epoch and marked fresh, so the refresh that mutation triggers is suppressed and the UI keeps pre-mutation data.

`if (refreshInFlight) return refreshInFlight` has NO epoch check while the near-miss guard added directly below it does, so a caller arriving after a mutation still joins a /me issued BEFORE it and receives pre-mutation data. INV-1 is only half enforced, in the very store the feature targets.

The new `if (s.loading) return` guard silently DROPS refetches, violating INV-1. `store/index.ts` wires sync:notification and sync:reconnect straight to this action, so an inbound frame landing during a load is discarded and the notification never appears; setPage/setUnreadOnly mutate page/unreadOnly then call it, so a page change or filter toggle is dropped leaving the UI on the new selection with the old items.

Deriving isAuthenticated from an UNVERIFIED persisted token means a revoked/deactivated (but not yet expired) token delivers AND initializes the whole authenticated-tier module surface before /auth/me proves anything, and loader.ts documents that modules are NEVER unloaded so the later failed verification cannot undo it.

Desktop contradiction inside the same change: bootSessionVerify.desktop.ts is a deliberate no-op because a token persisted from a previous desktop launch is stale BY CONSTRUCTION, yet hasLiveSession has no desktop twin and loadContext is shared — so on desktop that same guaranteed-invalid token now evaluates as a live session.

`expiresAt == null` is treated as a live session on token PRESENCE alone with no upper bound. seedSessionTokens writes expiresAt:null whenever a mint response omits expires_in, so this is the CURRENT shape too, not a legacy-only escape hatch, and localStorage is attacker-writable.

framework/package.json exports "./*": "./src/*", so an unconditional always-allow hasPermissionNow/evaluatePermission is a RESOLVABLE PUBLIC SUBPATH (@ziee/framework/__test-stubs__/permissions) for all three consuming apps, with no lint rule, files field, or build exclusion to prevent an import that silently bypasses every permission check.

The single-owner-proxy fix was applied only to the new-module branch; the DEV/HMR re-registration branch still destroys the old proxy and unconditionally builds a new one, so for a registerLazyStore store the proxy every consumer holds is destroyed and a second, independently ref-counted one installed — the exact double-init hazard the fix documents, left live on the surface developers actually run.

Registration silently flips to first-wins with no diagnostic, so a genuine name COLLISION (two different modules claiming one store name) is indistinguishable at runtime from the intended already-self-registered case and manifests as 'my store's actions do nothing'.

The coalescing key omits the RESOLVED BASE URL, which performCall obtains later via getBaseUrl() and which on desktop is a dynamic Tauri port that can change across a server restart — two callers straddling that change share one request aimed at the stale host. Every other request input is in the key; the origin is not.

__resetInflightForTests sets fetchEpoch = 0, moving a counter documented as monotonic BACKWARDS, so a previously-captured epoch (meFreshness.lastMeEpoch) can spuriously compare equal and report freshness for a different generation.

The exported `interface LazyDispatcher` collides by name with store-kit's already-exported `LazyDispatcher<L>` in the SAME package but has a completely different, fully-erased shape — two different public types under one name in one shared SDK is a guaranteed import mistake for the three consuming apps.
stableParams is documented as 'order-independent' but only sorts TOP-LEVEL entries, so a nested object's literal key order still changes the key. Neither stated as a limitation nor tested.

TAUTOLOGICAL acceptance test: TEST-6 [acceptance/INV-5] evaluates the test's OWN coldBootContext() with `can: () => false` hardcoded and never imports buildLoadContext, so its stated claim 'fails if permissions are ever persisted' is false — persisting them would leave the spec green. The only INV-5 acceptance test proves nothing about the shipped predicate.

TEST-12 mutates the SHARED admin fixture user's display name and restores it only at the very end of the body with no try/finally, so any earlier failure or timeout leaves the fixture user renamed for every subsequent spec in the run.

MAX_BACKOFF_MS is re-declared locally instead of imported from the module under test, so the 'never exceeds MAX_BACKOFF_MS' assertion keeps passing against a stale copy if the source constant changes — the exact regression the test exists to catch.

Silent self-weakening: if the sdk submodule is not initialised the ENTIRE submodule tree (where most of the diff lives) is skipped and all four tests still pass; the 'diff is non-empty' backstop counts superproject files only, so it cannot detect the degraded mode.

TEST-10a only asserts the happy case (drop a second IDENTICAL concurrent caller) and has no case where the second call's INTENT differs (setPage/setUnreadOnly mutate state then call load()), which is exactly where the new guard loses a required request — the test certifies the change while stepping around its defect.

The 'non-serializable args are never merged' spec only exercises a CYCLIC object — the one case JSON.stringify actually throws on — so the callback-collision the implementation's comment claims to handle is untested, and the stated contract is untrue.

Phantom leg: TEST-3 is named 'a sync frame invalidates joinability' but no sync frame exists — it calls bumpFetchEpoch() by hand and re-proves TEST-2's epoch comparison. Nothing tests that SyncClient.handleFrame/maybeResync actually bump BEFORE emitting, nor that callAsync's non-GET finally bumps.

An app-level auth module builds its own suppression policy on top of the shared transport's epoch counter, so any change to when the framework bumps silently changes /me freshness in the app with no compile-time coupling.

Invalidation granularity is a single GLOBAL epoch: one unrelated sync frame or any non-GET anywhere disables coalescing for every key at once, so the de-duplicator's hit rate is coupled to unrelated modules' write traffic. NOT FIXED — over-invalidation is the SAFE direction under INV-1; narrowing it is what would risk a stale join.

Every GET now performs an extra getAuthToken() (a synchronous localStorage read + JSON.parse under the default provider) plus params sort/stringify and an FNV pass over the ~800-char JWT, in addition to the identical getAuthToken() already done inside performCall.

SubscribeRefused is doc-commented as 'refused for capacity' but is thrown for EVERY non-ok status (401, 403, 500), misleading the reader of connectLoop into thinking refusedStatus !== null means capacity.
inflightSize() is exported and asserted on by the unit spec but has no production caller anywhere — it exists solely to make the spec assertable. Documented as a test/diagnostic seam.

INV-4 is upheld only textually: the transport coalescer is unconditional over all GETs so it also collapses GET /api/llm-models, the duplicate the concurrent agent owns. TEST-9 detects a textual reference, not a behavioural overlap. NOT FIXED — a per-endpoint carve-out in the transport would be exactly the hidden cross-module coupling the guidelines forbid; recorded in DEC-11 and reported explicitly instead.
